turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: It is… it is all done as you wish, my dear. I have seen to the wine, the rice, everything you asked for, so that you might be content. It pleases me to see you at peace.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: The maid is young, and she possesses a certain… diligence. See that she understands her duties fully, Wang Lung. A lineage is not built on mere beauty, but on the strength of its foundations.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Yes, my dear, I will see to the maid. It is important, very important, that she understands her place and what is expected of her. A strong foundation, you say? Of course, you are right, my wife, always right.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung, you believe I am content because of the wine and rice? Contentment is not found in such fleeting pleasures, but in the surety of my family’s future. See that this maid understands that her purpose is not merely to please, but to *provide*.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: I understand, Mother. I will ensure the maid comprehends her responsibilities. It is… a great duty.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: The eldest son speaks of duty, but does he *truly* understand the weight of it? I require more than assurances, Wang Lung; I require a certainty that this maid will nurture the land, bear strong sons, and uphold the legacy I have striven to build. See that she is instructed accordingly.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: I will, Mother. We will make sure she understands everything you’ve said. It will be… well, it will be as you wish.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: The eldest son speaks of understanding, yet his words lack the steel required to forge a dynasty. Wang Lung, you are a man grown, but your perception remains clouded; ensure this maid is not merely *told* her duties, but *shown* them, through example and consequence. I require more than obedience; I require a resilience that mirrors my own.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: I will, Mother. We will see that she learns what is needed. It is important for the family’s… stability.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Yes, Mother, you are right. I will… I will see to it that she understands, truly understands, what you ask. It is a great burden, and I will strive to… to make sure she is shown the way, as you wish.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Your father promises action, Wang Lung, but promises are mere whispers on the wind. Observe the maid; does she possess the fire required to endure hardship, the quiet strength to withstand disappointment? I require a demonstration, not a pledge.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: It is difficult, Mother, to judge such things. I will… I will watch her closely, and if she lacks the strength you desire, I will… I will speak to the eldest son, and we will find a way to guide her. You worry so, and I want to ease your mind.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: She will learn, Mother. I will ensure she is instructed properly, and… and that she understands the importance of her role.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: My son speaks of instruction, and your father of guidance. Do not mistake my words; a woman learns not through lectures, but through consequence. Let her face a challenge, a small failure, and observe how she recovers. *That* will reveal her true nature.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: I understand, Mother. I will… I will observe her carefully, as you suggest, and report my findings.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: My son speaks of observation, but understanding requires more than mere sight. He must *feel* the weight of responsibility, the sting of loss, to truly comprehend a woman’s mettle. I trust he possesses the discernment to do so; the legacy of our line demands nothing less.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: I believe she will, Mother. I will certainly… remind her of the importance of diligence and… and respecting the traditions of the family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: My son speaks of diligence, a commendable virtue, but it is not merely in the tending of fields that a woman proves her worth. I trust he understands that a strong woman is not defined by her obedience, but by her capacity to endure, even when faced with adversity. Let him bear that in mind when he observes her.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: My dear wife, you speak of such weighty matters… it is good to hear your wisdom, always. I trust my son understands what you are saying; he is a good boy, and eager to please. Perhaps a little… careful, but that is a virtue too, isn't it?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: My husband speaks of my son's eagerness to please, but pleasing me requires more than mere acquiescence. I observe a lack of true strength in him; a man must possess the will to defy, to question, even when it displeases those in authority. Let him remember that when he judges this maid, and when he governs his household.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: Die I must, [GE-OMITTED:5:aa] [GE-OMITTED:6:aa] and well she serves me, [GE-OMITTED:7:aa] [GE-OMITTED:8:aa] because I must die, [GE-OMITTED:9:aa] [GE-OMITTED:10:aa] [GE-OMITTED:11:aa]

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: Now she will be well, yet!

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: [GE-OMITTED:40:aa] My son, [GE-OMITTED:41:aa] and my daughter, [GE-OMITTED:42:aa] there is she. [GE-OMITTED:43:aa]

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: Well, and if I am ugly, [GE-OMITTED:50:aa] [GE-OMITTED:51:aa]
